title: Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) — Daily Observation
summary: The Effective Federal Funds Rate stood at 3.64% on April 15, 2026, unchanged from the prior four days. This daily observation reflects the interest rate at which depository institutions lend reserve balances to each other overnight.

why_it_matters: The EFFR serves as the primary monetary policy tool and benchmark for short-term borrowing costs. Sustained flat readings at 3.64% indicate unchanged Fed policy stance between FOMC meetings. This data point is useful for tracking rate stability but lacks context about recent FOMC decisions or forward guidance.
macro_context: The EFFR at 3.64% suggests the Fed's current restrictive policy stance remains in place. Without accompanying FOMC statement or economic data, the macro implications of this observation are unclear. This is a single daily snapshot, not indicative of a policy change.
market_structure_context: The EFFR is calculated as a weighted average of overnight federal funds transactions in the fed funds market, which is a core part of the Fed's monetary policy operating framework.
